title: Drag repaints the whole run on a full-res canvas and re-renders the entire ShotViewer tree on every pointer move
claim: A move or resize drag repaints the entire run containing the mark (all of its siblings) on a full-resolution canvas. Each move also calls `editShapes` -> `setShapes` in ShotViewer, re-rendering the whole ~1650-line tree (sidebar, ColorPicker, ClipMeta).
scenario: Dragging or resizing a mark on a large screenshot causes a full-res repaint and a full React re-render per pointermove, making interaction sluggish.
fix: During a drag, lift the dragged mark into its own layer (as is already done for drafts) and throttle with rAF; memoise the side panel.

votes.evidence: ShotAnnotate.tsx:796-802 onMove for a move drag calls `replace(state.id, {...}, state.gesture)` on every pointermove, and replace (701-705) is `onShapes(shapes.map(s => s.id === id ? {...s, ...patch} : s), gesture)`, so no rAF throttle and no local drag state. The layers are built by `toSteps(... shapes ...)` (679-682), which puts the new object into its existing run. The guard `sameLayer` (548-556) compares shape identities, so only the run holding the dragged mark fails it. That run's ShapeLayer effect (569-575) then runs `ctx.clearRect(0,0,element.width,element.height); paint(ctx, shapes)` on a canvas sized `width={width} height={height}` (picture resolution, 578-581), repainting every sibling in the run. The 'own layer' treatment in the comment at 670-673 only applies to `draft` (683), never to a dragged existing mark. On the ShotViewer side, onShapes={editShapes} (ShotViewer.tsx:888) calls `setShapes(after); setUnsaved(true);` (281-292) in the 1649-line ShotViewer component. ClipMeta (ClipMeta.tsx:16 `export function ClipMeta`) and ColorPicker are not memo-wrapped, and vite.config.ts uses plain `react()` with no React Compiler, so the whole panel reconciles on each move. usePictureBox's box is memoised (pictureBox.ts:96-99), so other runs really are skipped.
votes.reachable_by: Any user in draw mode who uses the Select tool to drag or resize an existing mark. The cost grows with picture resolution (4K stills) and with the number of marks in the same run.
votes.fix_assessment: Lifting the dragged mark out has to keep its z-order relative to later blur steps: split the run into before, dragged and after rather than putting it on top, which briefly adds full-res canvases. A rAF throttle adds little because Chromium already delivers pointermove at most once per frame. A simpler, larger win is to keep the drag local to AnnotateLayer (as is done for draft) and call onShapes once on pointerup, or else to memoise the side panel.

votes.evidence: ShotAnnotate.tsx:796-802 onMove 'move' branch calls replace(state.id, {...}, state.gesture) -> onShapes(shapes.map(...)) on every pointermove; ShotViewer.tsx:281-291 editShapes -> setShapes(after); setUnsaved(true) re-renders the whole ShotViewer (ClipMeta at :943, ColorPicker at :971/:984, neither memoised). ShotAnnotate.tsx:679-682 layers = useMemo(() => toSteps(...), [shapes, written]); toSteps (:491-524) groups consecutive non-blur marks into one {kind:'layer'} run; ShapeLayer (:566-575) clearRect + paint(ctx, shapes) on a canvas of the picture's full width/height. sameLayer (:548-556) compares marks by identity, and replace only rebuilds the touched mark, so ONLY the run containing the dragged mark repaints; the other runs are skipped. The 'layer of its own' treatment (:669-672, drawing at :684) applies to the draft only, not to move/resize drags. ShotViewer is mounted only in the main window (Clips.tsx:656), whose args in tauri.conf.json:27 keep the GPU (only overlay/console use --disable-gpu, overlay.rs:57).
votes.corrected_claim: The mechanism is real, but it is narrower than claimed. Each move or resize drag repaints one full-resolution canvas: the run holding the dragged mark and its non-blur neighbours. Other runs are skipped by sameLayer. Each move also re-renders ShotViewer and its unmemoised side panel. Chromium already aligns pointermove to animation frames, so this is at most one repaint and one React render per frame, not per raw sample. The canvas is GPU-accelerated in the main window. Expect visible lag only on weak hardware with a 4K still and a run holding many or long pen strokes. This is a low-severity performance issue, not a correctness one.
votes.reachable_by: Ordinary use by the local user: select tool, drag or resize an existing mark in the screenshot editor (main window, Clips route). No security impact.
votes.fix_assessment: Lifting the dragged mark into its own canvas during the gesture, as is done for drafts, would cut the repaint to that one mark, and memoising ClipMeta/side panel trims React work. An rAF throttle adds little because Chromium already coalesces pointermove per frame.

title: Failed thumbnail rebuild silently keeps the pre-edit (unredacted) thumbnail
claim: After an edit, thumbnail failure is only logged: `if let Err(err) = make_still(..) { log::warn!(..) }` (commands.rs:640-643), and `set_picture` (clips.rs:290-302) doesn't touch `thumb_path`. The old `thumbs/<id>.jpg` stays; gallery and console tiles use `?v=${clip.sizeBytes}`, which changes, so they re-fetch the old JPEG. Also, if the capture-time thumbnail failed, `thumb_path` stays NULL forever even after a successful rebuild.
scenario: ffmpeg is unavailable or fails at edit time (it was fine at capture): a 480-px thumbnail of the unblurred content remains visible in the gallery and console.
fix: Build the thumbnail in-process from the `picture` already in memory (box downscale + the existing `png` crate; drop the ffmpeg dependency for stills). On any failure delete the old thumbnail and set `thumb_path` to NULL. Have `set_picture` also set `thumb_path`.

votes.evidence: commands.rs:641-643 `if let Err(err) = crate::thumbs::make_still(&target, &clip.id) { log::warn!("thumbnail not refreshed: {err}"); }` then commands.rs:645-646 `lib.set_picture(&clip.id, picture.width, picture.height, size_bytes)`; clips.rs:289-301 set_picture only `UPDATE clips SET width = ?2, height = ?3, size_bytes = ?4` (thumb_path untouched; set_thumb at clips.rs:253 is only called from thumbs::migrate:115, which skips clips whose thumb_path is None at :89-91). thumbs.rs:50-62 make_still shells out to ffmpeg writing thumbs/<id>.jpg; a spawn failure (muxer.rs:66-68) leaves the old file in place. Reach: write_screenshot (commands.rs:497, invoked via ipc.ts:148 from ShotViewer.tsx:619) -> edit_screenshot -> write_picture (:598). Edits are not gated on ffmpeg readiness. tools.rs:135-156 sets TOOL_DIR only after the pinned VERSION is present/downloaded; until then muxer::tool falls back to bare 'ffmpeg' on PATH (muxer.rs:45-48). Tiles: Clips.tsx:474 and Console.tsx:633 `?v=${clip.sizeBytes}` re-fetch the same stale file. Dashboard.tsx:236 has no cache-buster at all. take_screenshot (state.rs:890-940) is not gated on ffmpeg, so a capture during the first-run download stores thumb_path=None (state.rs:933-939), and no later step records the thumbnail.
votes.corrected_claim: Exposure is local only. Screenshots cannot be shared as links (links.rs:343-345), so the stale thumbnail is never uploaded as a poster. A friend who receives a screenshot builds a thumbnail from the received file (share.rs:837-838). The unredacted original is also kept on disk by design (keep_original, commands.rs:605-619). The stale JPEG is a second local copy that the user can see in the UI, not a new exfiltration path.
votes.reachable_by: The local user, through ordinary use. They blur or crop a screenshot while the pinned ffmpeg is unavailable: the window after an app update that bumps tools::VERSION while the ~200 MB download runs or fails offline, a removed or quarantined ffmpeg.exe, or a failure writing the .jpg. The old 480-px thumbnail then keeps showing the unredacted content in the gallery, the console and the dashboard, visible to anyone who sees the screen (for example a stream of the main window). The NULL-forever part is reached by taking a screenshot before the first-run ffmpeg download finishes.
votes.fix_assessment: The fix is sound. Downscaling the in-memory picture in-process removes the ffmpeg dependency for stills. On any failure the code should delete thumbs/<id>.jpg and call set_thumb(None); on success it should call set_thumb(Some(path)), using the existing clips.rs:253, which also cures the NULL-forever case. Dashboard.tsx:236 also needs a ?v= cache-buster.

votes.evidence: commands.rs:641-643 `if let Err(err) = crate::thumbs::make_still(&target, &clip.id) { log::warn!("thumbnail not refreshed: {err}"); }`: the old file is neither deleted nor nulled. clips.rs:297-299 set_picture only runs `UPDATE clips SET width = ?2, height = ?3, size_bytes = ?4`, so thumb_path is never touched. thumbs.rs:51-63 make_still uses an external ffmpeg (muxer.rs:39-48 falls back to PATH if the pinned tool is missing), and on failure `thumbs/<id>.jpg` from capture is left in place. Capture: state.rs:933-939 sets `thumb_path` to None when make_still fails, and nothing ever repairs a NULL. thumbs.rs:91-93 migrate `continue`s on None, and set_thumb is called only from migrate. Consumers: Clips.tsx:474 and Console.tsx:633 use `${fileUrl(clip.thumbPath)}?v=${clip.sizeBytes}`, and size_bytes changes after the rewrite (commands.rs:640), so they re-fetch the stale JPEG. Dashboard.tsx:236 has no cache-buster at all. Exposure is limited to the local machine: share links refuse screenshots (links.rs:343-345 `if clip.screenshot { return Err(...) }`), so the poster upload at links.rs:487 never sends a screenshot thumbnail, and P2P receivers build their own thumbnail from the received file (share.rs:837-841).
votes.reachable_by: A local user who edits (blurs or crops) a screenshot while ffmpeg cannot be started or fails, for example the pinned binary was removed or quarantined, or the thumbnail file is locked. For the NULL thumb_path part: any screenshot taken while ffmpeg was unavailable, such as before the tool download finished. The stale image shows only in local UI (gallery, console overlay, dashboard, share dialog). It is never uploaded.
votes.fix_assessment: The robust core of the fix is sound: on failure, delete thumbs/<id>.jpg and set thumb_path to NULL, and on success set thumb_path. Building the thumbnail in-process needs care. The crate only has `png` (no JPEG encoder), while thumbs::path names the file `.jpg`, so either the path or extension changes or the code relies on content sniffing.

title: Editor trusts database dimensions when there is no original; received screenshots carry sender-claimed dimensions
claim: `screenshot_edit` falls back to `} else { (clip.width, clip.height) }` when there is no original (commands.rs:457-461). Received screenshots store sender-supplied meta as dimensions (`width: meta.width, height: meta.height`, share.rs:129-136, 841-851) without reading the file header.
scenario: A friend's screenshot with wrong meta: the canvas, `full` and the CropLayer are sized wrongly, and `object-contain` letterboxes the real image inside a box of the wrong aspect. Marks and blurs misalign, and Rust rejects layers ("does not fit").
fix: In `screenshot_edit` always use `size_of_png(clip.path)` when there is no original. At receive time verify the header (PNG magic, sane dimensions) and store the real dimensions.

votes.evidence: commands.rs:457-461 `let (original_width, original_height) = if original.is_file() { crate::shot::size_of_png(&original).unwrap_or((clip.width, clip.height)) } else { (clip.width, clip.height) };` -- no header read when there is no image.png. share.rs:848-849 file_clip: `width: meta.width, height: meta.height,` straight from the offer; offered() (share.rs:535-560) checks only id/sha256 lengths and tracks, never the dimensions or the file content. ShotViewer.tsx:426-429 `full = { width: edit?.originalWidth ?? clip.width, ... }` sizes CropLayer (:894-898) and the mark layers (:615 `layerBytes(step.shapes, full.width, full.height)`); the img is `object-contain` inside a box computed from ground.width/height (:840-852). On save, edit_screenshot calls keep_original then read_png(original) -> real dims, and shot.rs:104-107 `if top.0 != self.width || top.1 != self.height { return Err("The layer does not fit the picture.") }`; blur coordinates are applied in the real picture's frame, so they land in the wrong place.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated, with two scope notes. (1) It is transient: keep_original (commands.rs:606-620) runs before the failing read, so after the first save attempt image.png exists and the next screenshot_edit uses size_of_png(original); a successful blur/crop-only save also corrects the DB via set_picture (commands.rs:646). So the first edit session is the broken one: layers are rejected, or blurs/crops land in the wrong place. (2) An honest ClippiBoy sender sends its own DB dimensions (share.rs:267-268), which match the file unless the file was changed outside ClippiBoy. The same stale-DB fallback therefore also hits LOCAL screenshots cropped in another app (the case under_rect's comment at shot.rs:398-401 anticipates). View mode also sizes the stage from clip.width/height (ShotViewer.tsx:449).
votes.reachable_by: A friend whose client sends wrong width/height in the offer meta (a modified or buggy client), after the user accepts the offer; or any screenshot whose file was cropped or resized outside ClippiBoy (local, or sent on by an honest sender), opened in the editor before any ClippiBoy edit.
votes.fix_assessment: Reading the header with size_of_png(clip.path) when there is no original is cheap and fixes every source of stale dimensions, including external edits. Checking the header at receive time and storing the real dimensions is a useful addition, and the DB width/height should also be corrected, because view mode uses them too.

votes.evidence: commands.rs:457-461 `if original.is_file() { size_of_png(&original).unwrap_or((clip.width, clip.height)) } else { (clip.width, clip.height) }`; share.rs:848-849 `width: meta.width, height: meta.height` (file_clip, no header read); ShotViewer.tsx:427 `width: edit?.originalWidth ?? clip.width`, :448 view mode `{ src: clip.path, width: clip.width, height: clip.height }`, :615 `layerBytes(step.shapes, full.width, full.height)`; shot.rs:106-107 blend `if top.0 != self.width || top.1 != self.height { Err("The layer does not fit the picture.") }`. Honest senders: share.rs:267-268 send `clip.width/clip.height`, which are the real PNG size (state.rs:950-951 from the grabbed shot; commands.rs:646 `set_picture(picture.width, picture.height)` after every edit). Self-heal: commands.rs:523 `keep_original(&clip)?` runs before the failing blend at :578, so the next screenshot_edit finds image.png and uses size_of_png. Entry: server/src/hub.ts:256 relays only between friends; share.rs:526-534 accept_clips gate; user must press Accept (share_accept, share.rs:360).
votes.corrected_claim: The mechanism is real: an untouched received screenshot is sized in the editor and viewer from the sender-supplied meta.width/height, and Rust rejects mark layers when they don't match. But a stock ClippiBoy sender always sends the true PNG size, so this needs a modified or third-party client run by an accepted friend, and the user has to accept the offer. It also corrects itself. The first save attempt (even one that fails at blend) runs keep_original first, so on the next open screenshot_edit reads the real size from image.png. Any successful save then fixes the database dimensions through set_picture. Until then, view mode and crop letterbox wrongly, and a crop made in the bad coordinates is clamped and can cut the wrong region.
votes.reachable_by: Only a friend (mutual friendship enforced by the server at hub.ts:256) running a modified or non-stock client who sends lying meta, and only after the user accepts the offer under their accept_clips setting. Ordinary use with stock senders never triggers it. In practice it is unlikely, and the only harm is to that one received picture.
votes.fix_assessment: The fix is sound and cheap. Using size_of_png(clip.path) when there is no original removes the editor dependency on the database. Reading the PNG header in file_clip (and storing the real size, or rejecting the file) also fixes view mode and the library dimensions.

title: Received screenshots may be JPEG, which permanently breaks editing and Copy picture
claim: The receive path accepts `jpg/jpeg` for screenshots (share.rs:1187-1190), but the editor and clipboard assume PNG.
scenario: For a received `.jpg` screenshot, `keep_original` copies the JPEG to `image.png`, after which `read_png` fails forever; Copy picture also fails.
fix: At receive time verify the header (PNG magic, sane dimensions) and reject non-PNG screenshots.

votes.evidence: share.rs:1187-1190 `"mp4" | "mkv" | "mov" | "webm" | "png" | "jpg" | "jpeg" => ext` with no check against meta.screenshot; receive (share.rs:643) saves under that name and file_clip (share.rs:864) sets `screenshot: meta.screenshot` with no content check. The thumbnail uses ffmpeg (thumbs.rs:51-63), so the item looks normal. Edit: commands.rs:523 keep_original copies the file to image.png (shot.rs:288), then :539 `read_png(original_path)` fails on JPEG data (png::Decoder, shot.rs:455-466), and has_original stays true, so every later edit fails the same way (forget is only reached on success, :535). Copy picture: commands.rs:666 `read_png(clip.path)` fails directly. Honest senders never produce this: state.rs:1232 `let extension = if kind == ClipKind::Screenshot { "png" } ...`, and write_picture (commands.rs:632-634) keeps the path and writes PNG.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated. The scope is a bit wider: no content check runs for screenshot=true at all, so a file named .mp4 or holding arbitrary bytes, flagged as a screenshot, breaks editing and Copy picture the same way. The copy into image.png is not what causes the failure (read_png on the JPEG fails either way); it just makes the failure persist. Stock ClippiBoy never sends a JPEG screenshot, so only a modified or third-party sender can reach this.
votes.reachable_by: Only an accepted friend (hub.ts:256 areFriends) running a non-stock client who flags a JPEG (or any non-PNG) file as a screenshot, and only after the user accepts the offer. A stock app never does this. The impact is limited to that one received item: viewing and the thumbnail work, editing and Copy picture fail with an error. There is no crash and no effect on other clips.
votes.fix_assessment: Checking the PNG magic and size at receive time, keyed on meta.screenshot rather than the extension, closes it and also covers the .mp4 or garbage case. Dropping jpg/jpeg from safe_file_name alone would not be enough.

votes.evidence: share.rs:1187-1190 `"mp4" | "mkv" | "mov" | "webm" | "png" | "jpg" | "jpeg" => ext,` -- the screenshot flag and the extension are never cross-checked, and receive() (share.rs:618-680) only checks the sender-supplied sha256, never the content. edit_screenshot: keep_original copies clip.path to image.png (commands.rs:617), then `crate::shot::read_png(&crate::shot::original_path(&clip.id))?` (:533/:539). read_png uses png::Decoder::read_info (shot.rs:455-467), which fails with InvalidSignature on non-PNG data (png-0.17.16 decoder/stream.rs:810-820). copy_clip_image: `crate::shot::read_png(std::path::Path::new(&clip.path))?` (commands.rs:666). A locally captured screenshot is always .png (state.rs:1232 `let extension = if kind == ClipKind::Screenshot { "png" } else { "mp4" };`).
votes.corrected_claim: A received screenshot whose bytes are not PNG can never be edited (crop, marks or reset) and Copy picture always fails for it, because read_png only decodes PNG. Two details are wrong. (1) Nothing breaks 'permanently' because of keep_original: read_png fails on the very first attempt whether or not image.png exists, and the copy only leaves a misnamed JPEG in the edit store that is cleared when the clip is deleted. (2) The jpg/jpeg allowlist entry is not the root cause. Content is never checked, so a screenshot named .png that holds JPEG (or any other) bytes, or one sent with a .mp4 name, fails the same way. An honest ClippiBoy sender never produces this, because its screenshots are always PNG.
votes.reachable_by: A friend whose client is modified or not ClippiBoy (or who passes on such a file) sends an offer with screenshot:true and non-PNG content, and the receiving user accepts it.
votes.fix_assessment: Checking the content at receive time (PNG signature plus a successful read_info with sane dimensions) and rejecting non-PNG screenshots is the right fix. It must not rely on the extension, and for screenshots the stored extension should be forced to .png.

title: AnnotateLayer and CropLayer never clear an interrupted drag
claim: AnnotateLayer only handles pointer down/move/up (ShotAnnotate.tsx:917-925), and `onMove` never checks `event.buttons` (764-767); CropLayer (ShotViewer.tsx:1408-1414) has the same gap. The stage's own pan handler already handles the case ("Let go somewhere the stage never heard of it (Alt+Tab mid-drag)", ShotViewer.tsx:786-790), but the two layers don't.
scenario: After Alt+Tab or a lost pointer capture mid-drag, `drag.current` or `draft` stays set; the selected mark (or the crop) follows the hovering mouse with no button held and keeps adding to the same undo step until the next click.
fix: Add `onPointerCancel` and `onLostPointerCapture` handlers that reset `drag.current` and the draft, and ignore moves with `event.buttons === 0`.

votes.evidence: src/components/ShotAnnotate.tsx:923-925 the layer div wires only `onPointerDown={onDown} onPointerMove={onMove} onPointerUp={onUp}`; handles (967-983) likewise only down/move/up. onMove (764-765) `const state = drag.current; const point = at(event);` then acts on state/draft with no `event.buttons` check; drag.current is cleared only in onUp (857) and the handle's onPointerUp (982); draft only via setDraft(null) in onUp (868). No pointercancel/lostpointercapture/blur/visibility handler anywhere in either file (grep). CropLayer src/components/ShotViewer.tsx:1411-1413, 1429-1431, 1447-1449: only down/move/up; onMove 1367-1369 `if (!state) return;` then onRect(...) with no buttons check; drag.current=null only in onUp 1391. Contrast the stage pan handler ShotViewer.tsx:786-790 `// Let go somewhere the stage never heard of it (Alt+Tab mid-drag). if (event.buttons === 0) { pan.current = null; return; }` plus 802-803 onPointerCancel/onLostPointerCapture. Undo coalescing: ShotViewer.tsx:285 `if (gesture === undefined || gesture !== lastGesture.current) history.current.push(before)` so stale move/handle drags with the same `drag-N` gesture merge into one undo step.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate in substance, with two refinements: (1) only stale move/handle drags of a mark (drag.current) write marks and merge into the drag's undo step; a stale draft (new mark) just follows the mouse uncommitted and is silently replaced by the next pointerdown's setDraft (ShotAnnotate.tsx:747), and the crop selection (setSel) has no undo history at all. (2) The next click clears it (pointerup resets drag.current). Whether WebView2 really withholds pointerup/pointercancel after Alt+Tab mid-drag is platform behaviour not checkable here, but the codebase's own pan handler comment at ShotViewer.tsx:786 states it was observed.
votes.reachable_by: The local user dragging a mark, a mark handle, a new mark or the crop rectangle and then Alt+Tabbing (or otherwise losing the Win32 mouse capture) before releasing the button; no remote trigger.
votes.fix_assessment: Sound and consistent with the existing pan handler: add onPointerCancel/onLostPointerCapture that clear drag.current (and setDraft(null) or commit it) on the layer, the handles and the crop elements, and bail out of onMove when event.buttons === 0. Note the handles call setPointerCapture on their own element, so lostpointercapture must be handled there too.

title: Unredacted original kept forever in originals/<id>/image.png with no way to purge it
claim: The pre-edit original is stored at `%APPDATA%\ClippiBoy\originals\<id>\image.png` (shot.rs:287-289) indefinitely. `discard_original` (edit.rs:139-151) only knows `video.mp4` and returns "There is no original to throw away." for screenshots, so the only way to purge the unredacted pixels is to delete the screenshot.
scenario: A user blurs or crops sensitive content believing it is gone; the unredacted full image remains on disk in the app data folder with no UI to remove it.
fix: Add a "Flatten - discard history" action that removes `image.png`, `base.png` and `shot.json` (keeping `under.*`). Mention in the UI that blur and crop stay reversible locally.

votes.evidence: src-tauri/src/shot.rs:287-289 `pub fn original_path(clip_id) -> PathBuf { crate::edit::dir(clip_id).join("image.png") }`; edit.rs:56-62 dir = config::data_dir().join("originals").join(id), config.rs:10-12 data_dir = dirs::data_dir()/ClippiBoy (%APPDATA%\ClippiBoy). commands.rs edit_screenshot calls `keep_original(&clip)?` unconditionally for every edit (blur/marks too, not only crop) and keep_original `std::fs::copy(&clip.path, &original)` once. The only removal paths: shot::forget (shot.rs:433-437), reached only when `crop.is_none() && steps.is_empty() && marks.is_empty()` i.e. reverting the file to the unredacted original (commands.rs ~531-536), and edit::remove on delete_clip. edit.rs:139-143 `let video = video_path(clip_id); if !video.is_file() { return Err("There is no original to throw away.".into()); }` and trim_originals_on_disk (160-180) only counts video.mp4. UI: 'Free up space…' needs clip.originalAvailable (clipMenu.tsx:223), which is edit::has_original = trim note + video.mp4 (edit.rs:97-99, clips.rs:145), always false for a screenshot.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate. Two nuances: the original is kept for any edit (blur-only included), not only a crop as the shot.rs:281 doc says; and the UI already discloses the kept copy ('Edited — the untouched picture sits beside it' pill tooltip, ShotViewer.tsx:743, and 'The untouched picture is kept beside it…' in the crop panel, ShotViewer.tsx:1181), so the 'believes it is gone' scenario is only partly true. The shared/exported file (clip.path) is redacted; the exposure is local (app-data folder, roaming profile/backups). under.png also holds unblurred pixels of the watermark corner.
votes.reachable_by: Anyone with read access to the user's %APPDATA%\ClippiBoy\originals folder (other local users with access, backups, roaming-profile sync, malware); the user cannot purge it short of deleting the screenshot or reverting the redaction.
votes.fix_assessment: A 'flatten / discard history' action deleting image.png, base.png and shot.json is workable (the next edit would re-snapshot the redacted file via keep_original), but it should also consider under.png/under.json, which can contain unblurred pixels under the watermark and whose size check (under_rect) will reject them after a crop anyway.

title: Undo merges drags across an AnnotateLayer remount because gesture ids restart at 0
claim: Gesture ids come from `gestures.current`, which restarts at 0 whenever AnnotateLayer remounts (draw -> crop -> Cancel -> draw), while `lastGesture` in ShotViewer survives the remount. The first drag afterwards (`drag-1`) therefore merges with the last drag before the remount (`drag-1`).
scenario: User drags a mark, switches to crop, cancels, returns to draw and drags again; one Undo reverts both drags.
fix: Use a module-level or `useId`-based gesture counter and reset `lastGesture` on mode change.

votes.evidence: src/components/ShotAnnotate.tsx:638 `const gestures = useRef(0);` (per-instance, resets on mount); :735 and :976 `gesture: \`drag-${++gestures.current}\``. src/components/ShotViewer.tsx:880-891 `{mode === "draw" && (<AnnotateLayer ... onShapes={editShapes} />)}` so the layer unmounts in crop mode; pickPreset (ShotViewer.tsx:540-549) sets mode "crop" and leaveCrop (567-571) `setMode(unsaved ? At the maximum the halo is about 12*base*scale, around 27 screen px at fit-to-window on any resolution, and it grows with editor zoom because the margin is fixed in picture pixels.

title: Blur edge handling differs between preview and file

also.title: Rust blur edge semantics assume backdrop-filter behaviour that may not hold

also.fix: Verify in WebView2; add parity tests / single renderer.

votes.evidence: Rust reads beyond the rectangle: src-tauri/src/shot.rs:156-161 `let from_x = left.saturating_sub(radius); ... let to_x = (left + w + radius).min(self.width as usize);`. It also blurs the UNCROPPED original and crops only afterwards: src-tauri/src/commands.rs:569-584 `let mut picture = pristine; for step in &steps { ... picture.blur(...) ... } if let Some(area) = crop { picture = picture.crop(...)?; }`. So at a crop edge the preview's backdrop holds either black stage or nothing beyond the ground, while the file blurs in the real pixels that the crop later removes. The shot.rs:129-134 comment's premise that the preview 'blurs the whole picture and clips afterwards' is a claim about Chromium that cannot be checked here.
votes.corrected_claim: The crop-edge mismatch follows from the source alone: the core blurs the pre-crop original, while the preview only has the cropped ground on a black stage. The broader claim that blur edges differ at every patch edge, because Chromium/WebView2 clips the backdrop to the element and mirrors at its edge, rests on Chromium's backdrop-filter edge mode and cannot be verified from this repo. If it holds, the file is the more blurred one at patch edges, which is the safe direction for redaction.

votes.fix_assessment: There is no concrete fix. Aligning the two means either the core blurs after cropping and clamps or mirrors at the rectangle like Chromium, or the preview shows the core-rendered blur. Either needs a WebView2 check first.

title: Caption text jumps vertically on commit (CSS line-height vs canvas textBaseline top)
claim: The caption edit field uses `lineHeight: 1.25` (CSS half-leading) while the canvas draws with `textBaseline = "top"` (em-box top), so the two place text at different vertical offsets.
scenario: Text moves a few pixels vertically when the caption is committed from the field to the canvas.
fix: No specific fix given (align the field's line box with the canvas baseline).

also.title: Possible vertical jump when a caption is put down
also.claim: The in-place caption textarea's CSS line box uses line-height 1.25 (ShotAnnotate.tsx:1019-1020) while the canvas draws text with `textBaseline="top"` (248), so the text may jump vertically when the caption is committed. The report says to verify in WebView2.
also.fix: Position both the textarea and canvas text from `fontBoundingBoxAscent`.

votes.evidence: Canvas: src/components/ShotAnnotate.tsx:247-258 `ctx.font = textFont(shape.size); ctx.textBaseline = "top"; ... const y = y1 + at * shape.size * LINE_HEIGHT; ctx.fillText(line, x1, y);` Field: ShotAnnotate.tsx:1013-1020 `...css(typing.x, typing.y), font: `600 ${style.size * box.scale}px Inter, ...`, lineHeight: LINE_HEIGHT` with p-0 (1011) and no vertical correction anywhere (no fontBoundingBox*/half-leading code in src/). In CSS the first baseline sits at half-leading + ascent = LH/2 + (A-D)/2 em below the field's top. Canvas 'top' places the em-square top at y (Blink: NormalizedTypoAscent, about tA/(tA+tD) em). These agree only by coincidence: a font with A+D = 1 em is off by exactly the half-leading, 0.125 em. With Inter-like metrics (A~0.969, D~0.241) it is about 0.19 em. While a caption is being edited it is left off the canvas (678-681), so on commit the field disappears and the canvas text appears at the other offset.
votes.reachable_by: Every caption typed or re-edited in the editor. The size of the jump depends on the font that actually resolves (Inter / Segoe UI Variable Display via the local() @font-face in src/index.css:5-11): roughly 0.1-0.3 em, a few screen pixels at the default size.
votes.fix_assessment: Offsetting the textarea by (canvas em-top baseline - CSS first baseline), measured once with measureText().fontBoundingBoxAscent / emHeightAscent, or drawing with textBaseline='alphabetic' at y + half-leading + ascent, would align them. The suggested fontBoundingBoxAscent approach works if both sides use it.

The UI lets a crop go down to 16 px wide: ShotViewer.tsx:63 `const MIN_EDGE = 16;`, enforced only at :1387 `rect.width < MIN_EDGE || rect.height < MIN_EDGE`. After an edit, commands.rs:641 `if let Err(err) = crate::thumbs::make_still(&target, &clip.id) { log::warn!("thumbnail not refreshed: {err}"); }`, so a failure is only logged. A previously existing .jpg kept the same md5, so the old thumbnail stays (stale). 16x2160 gives 480x64800, just under the limit. 16x16 gives 480x480, so it is upscaled.

It handles all three cases: 16x3000 gives 3x480, 16x2160 gives 4x480, and 16x16 stays 16x16. Because Command passes the args without a shell, the quotes reach ffmpeg's filter parser as intended. title: Out-of-range rectangles are clamped to a 1-pixel strip instead of rejected
claim: Clamping uses `x.min(self.width.saturating_sub(1))`, so a rectangle entirely right of or below the picture becomes a 1-px strip at the edge: `clamped` and `crop` succeed and `blur` writes one column, instead of returning an error. The UI never sends such a rect, but a buggy or compromised caller could.
scenario: A malformed write_screenshot call with a rect outside the picture silently crops to / blurs a 1-px edge strip rather than failing.
fix: `if area.x >= self.width || area.y >= self.height { return Err(..) }`.

For area.x >= self.width this gives x = width-1 and width = 1, so no error. crop at shot.rs:60-63 and blur at :148-151 repeat the same logic, so blur writes a 1-column (or 1-row) strip at the edge, and a non-ellipse blur copies it back at :195-196. commands.rs:551 `Some(area) => Some(pristine.clamped(area)?)` and :563/:583 crop to that 1-px strip, base.png and shot.json record it, and write_picture overwrites the clip file with it. The test named `a_rectangle_beside_the_picture_is_no_rectangle` (shot.rs:811-815) only checks `width: 0`, so a rect that really is beside the picture is never tested. The UI does not produce one: ShotAnnotate.tsx:694-697 clamps the pointer to [0,width]/[0,height], :509 drops blurs <2 px, and the crop UI enforces MIN_EDGE.

title: Size slider steps from a fractional minimum, so values snap off the default
claim: The slider uses `step = 1` (Controls.tsx:95) with `range()` min `Math.max(1, base*0.4)` (ShotAnnotate.tsx:127), which can be fractional (e.g. 0.8 or 3.2), so values snap to 0.8, 1.8 …
scenario: The slider knob shows a value different from the default size until it is touched.
fix: Pass `step = min` or round `min`.

votes.evidence: Controls.tsx:95 `step = 1,` passed to `<input type="range" ... min={min} step={step}>` (108-114). ShotAnnotate.tsx:114-115 `baseStroke = Math.max(2, Math.round(width / 480))` and :127 `return [Math.max(1, base * 0.4), base * 6, base];`. ShotViewer.tsx:997-1002 `<Slider value={style.size} min={sizeRange[0]} max={sizeRange[1]} ...>` with no step; the label at 1004 shows `Math.round(style.size)`.
votes.corrected_claim: The mechanism is right, but the example 0.8 cannot occur: base is at least 2, and Math.max(1, 0.8) gives 1. min is fractional when base is 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and so on, for example 1.2 at 1280 wide, 1.6 at 1920 wide and 3.2 at 3840 wide. With step 1 and the step base at min, the grid is 1.6, 2.6, 3.6 and so on, so the default 4 is shown at 3.6 (8 at 3840 wide is shown at 8.2). The label reads 4 and the gradient fill is computed from 4. After the slider is touched, sizes become x.6, the exact default can no longer be reached, and the reachable maximum is 23.6, not 24.
votes.reachable_by: Any user opening the editor on a typical 1920- or 3840-wide screenshot with the arrow, box, ellipse or pen tool.
votes.fix_assessment: Rounding min (for example Math.max(1, Math.round(base * 0.4))) puts every default on the integer grid and fixes it. 'step = min' would not: the grid 1.6, 3.2, 4.8 still misses the default 4.

title: Redaction blur written to the file is much weaker than the preview shows
claim: The saved PNG gets a single box-blur pass per axis (`blur_rows(&patch, &mut across, pw, ph, radius); … blur_rows(&turned, &mut done, ph, pw, radius);` in shot.rs), while the preview is a CSS Gaussian of the same variance (`backdropFilter: blur(${sigmaOf(step.radius) * box.scale}px)` with `Math.sqrt((radius*(radius+1))/3)` in ShotAnnotate.tsx). Matching variance does not match legibility: a box kernel has sinc side-lobes, a Gaussian none. For r = 4/8/16 (the 1080p minimum and default) the box lets through about 22% of contrast at periods of 6.3/11.9/23 px versus about 3.5% for the equal-variance Gaussian (roughly 6x less) - exactly text-stroke and letter scale. title: Save-path failures other than writeScreenshot are swallowed in ShotViewer
claim: The save catch is `catch { /* "The notice is already in the store." */ }`, which is true only for `writeScreenshot`. A throw in `layerBytes` (`getContext`/`toBlob` returning null) or in the follow-up `screenshotEdit` shows nothing.
scenario: Layer encoding fails (e.g. at 8K) or the reload after save fails: no error is shown and the UI stays "unsaved" although the file may have been written.
fix: Set `lastError` in that catch for non-writeScreenshot failures.

Only src/store.ts:602-607 sets `lastError` (writeScreenshot path). BUT the only consumer of lastError is src/routes/settings/index.tsx:40,80 (`{lastError && (<Card ...>{lastError}</Card>)}`), and write_screenshot (src-tauri/src/commands.rs:498-508) never calls crate::notify, so no toast either (Toasts.tsx only listens to the backend "notice" event).

So the comment 'The notice is already in the store' is technically true for writeScreenshot but nothing in the viewer shows it. 'The file may have been written' applies only to the screenshotEdit-after-success case; a layerBytes throw happens before writeScreenshot, so nothing is written then.
votes.reachable_by: Any user saving marks/crop when canvas encoding fails (rare; depends on WebView2 canvas limits/memory, not checkable here), when screenshot_edit fails after a successful write (e.g. clip deleted meanwhile), or any write_screenshot error (disk, locked file, out-of-range coordinates).

title: Temp-file names collide across concurrent saves and leftovers are never cleaned up
claim: The main PNG temp is `target.with_extension(format!("{}.new.png", std::process::id()))` (commands.rs:633) and shot.json uses a fixed `shot.json.part` (shot.rs:353). Two concurrent saves of the same clip in one process write the same temp files, and nothing ever cleans up leftovers.

title: Pen strokes copy the whole points array per sample and miss coalesced events
claim: Pen strokes copy the whole points array on every sample (O(n^2)) and don't use `getCoalescedEvents()`, so fast strokes come out angular. `bounds()` uses `Math.min(...xs)` spreads, which can hit V8's argument limit on extremely long strokes (speculative).
scenario: Long pen strokes get progressively slower; fast strokes look jagged; an extremely long stroke could throw from `bounds()`.
fix: Append points without copying, use `getCoalescedEvents()`, and compute bounds with a loop instead of spread.

votes.evidence: ShotAnnotate.tsx:849-852: `const last = points[points.length - 1]; if (last && Math.hypot(point.x - last[0], point.y - last[1]) * box.scale < 1) return; setDraft({ ...draft, points: [...points, [point.x, point.y]] });`. 683: `drawing = useMemo(() => (draft ? toSteps([draft]) : []), [draft])`, so ShapeLayer 573-574 runs clearRect plus paint() on every new draft, and paint 240 re-strokes the whole path (`points.slice(1)`). No getCoalescedEvents anywhere in src/. bounds() 316-322 and move drag 794 use `Math.min(...xs)` spreads.
votes.corrected_claim: Points are not appended on every sample. A sample closer than one displayed pixel to the last point is dropped (line 851). For accepted samples the array is copied (O(n) each), but every accepted sample also clears the full-resolution draft canvas and re-strokes the whole path, which is also O(n). So the progressive slowdown comes mostly from the repaint, not the copy, and appending without copying alone would not remove it. getCoalescedEvents is indeed not used, so with Chromium's frame-aligned pointermove a fast stroke is a polyline of per-frame samples (a runtime-dependent effect). The spread limit in bounds() would need a single stroke of roughly 100k or more points, each at least one display pixel apart, which is practically unreachable.
votes.reachable_by: A user drawing long or fast freehand pen strokes in the screenshot editor.
votes.fix_assessment: getCoalescedEvents() would help stroke fidelity, and loop-based bounds are a harmless hardening. Real scaling would need incremental drawing of only the new segment on the draft canvas (keeping points in a ref), not just avoiding the array copy.

title: Watermark scale() degenerates when upscaling, producing a blocky mark unlike the smooth preview
claim: `scale()` in watermark.rs:179-205 assumes downscaling. For frames taller than about 2171 px (152/0.07, e.g. 5K, 8K or tall crops) it degenerates to nearest/box sampling, so the burned-in mark is blocky while the `` preview is smooth.
scenario: Saving a 5K/8K screenshot or a tall crop produces a visibly blocky watermark that differs from the preview.
fix: Use bilinear sampling when `step < 1`.

votes.evidence: src-tauri/src/watermark.rs:184-188 `let top = (target_y as f32 * step_y) as u32; let bottom = (((target_y + 1) as f32 * step_y).ceil() as u32).clamp(top + 1, height);` (same for x), then an unweighted mean (200-201). It really is a downscale-only area filter. With step < 1 it averages 1 or 2 source rows/columns per target pixel, with equal weights. A float32 simulation of these exact windows on the real 535x152 PNG gives: 5K (frame 2880, mark 202 px) windows (0,1),(0,2),(1,3),(2,4),(3,4),(3,5)... are mostly 2-pixel averages, so the result is soft, not blocky. 8K (4320, mark 302 px) windows (0,1),(0,2),(1,2),(1,3),... are s0, avg(s0,s1), s1, avg(s1,s2), which is a 2x linear interpolation. Alpha against PIL bilinear: mean |diff| 0.42% / 0.32%, p99 10% / 7.5%. Pure pixel duplication (nearest) happens only at exact integer ratios, e.g. mark height 304 (frame 4336-4349, reachable through a crop of an 8K shot): p99 16%. The preview (ShotViewer.tsx:905-919) is the PNG in an scaled by the browser. Upscaling starts at frame height >= 2179 (round(h*0.07) >= 153), not 2171; 4K (2160) still gives 151 (test at watermark.rs:245).
votes.corrected_claim: scale() is a box filter meant for shrinking. When it enlarges (frame height >= ~2179 px) it averages 1-2 neighbouring source pixels with equal weights, so the mark is placed slightly off (sub-pixel) and comes out a little softer or uneven compared with bilinear. It is NOT visibly blocky at 5K or 8K: at 8K the windows amount to 2x linear interpolation. Only at exact integer ratios (e.g. a 304 px mark) does it become pure pixel doubling, and even then the difference is small on an anti-aliased source. 'Tall crops' cannot trigger it on their own: a crop is never taller than its source.
votes.reachable_by: Screenshots (fresh via stamp() or edited via stamp_kept()) whose height is at least ~2179 px: 5K/6K/8K displays, portrait 4K monitors, or crops of those.
votes.fix_assessment: Switching to bilinear when step < 1 (keeping the area average for shrinking) would be marginally more exact, but the visible gain is small. This is polish, not a bug fix.

title: ShotViewer.tsx is a 1650-line component holding too much state
claim: ShotViewer.tsx (about 1650 lines) holds the viewer, the load/save state machine, undo history, crop layer, side panel, Disclosure/PanelButton and `layerBytes`. Several bugs (ED-4, ED-5, ED-6) stem from that state being spread across closures.
scenario: Race and state bugs are hard to see and fix; the whole tree re-renders on edits.
fix: Extract `useShotEdit(id)` (load, save, race guards, busy, error), `useUndoHistory`, `CropLayer.tsx`, `AnnotatePanel.tsx`, and a `layers.ts` (render and encode).

votes.evidence: `wc -l src/components/ShotViewer.tsx` = 1649. But the ShotViewer component itself is lines 147-1270 (~1120 lines); the file also holds separate top-level pieces: ratioOf :90, fitRatio :103, `function CropLayer` :1280-1456 (already its own component with its own refs, e.g. :1297 `const drag = useRef`), readMarks :1464, shift :1475, defaultStyles :1488, Disclosure :1517, PanelButton :1566, layerBytes :1607, Step :1626. Inside ShotViewer: ~20 useState (:160-198) plus history/current/lastGesture refs (:256-264) and the load/save closure `write` (:604-644). The annotation layer lives in ShotAnnotate.tsx, where ShapeLayer is `memo` (:566) and layers are `useMemo` (:679-683), so a mark edit re-renders ShotViewer but does not repaint unchanged canvases.
votes.corrected_claim: The file is ~1650 lines, but the ShotViewer component is ~1120 lines; CropLayer, Disclosure, PanelButton and layerBytes are already separate functions/components in the same file (moving them out is mostly a file split). The component does hold the load/save state machine, undo history and ~20 pieces of state, and the save continuation in `write` (ShotViewer.tsx:604-644) is where ED-5/ED-6 live, so the maintainability point stands; 'the whole tree re-renders' is mitigated by the memoised ShapeLayer in ShotAnnotate.tsx.
votes.reachable_by: Maintainers; no user-visible behaviour on its own.
votes.fix_assessment: A `useShotEdit(id)` hook that owns load/save with a clip-id guard would directly address ED-4/ED-5; moving CropLayer/Disclosure/PanelButton/layerBytes into their own files is cheap but changes little by itself.

title: Each editor mode decodes a different full-resolution PNG in the WebView
claim: View, draw and crop modes each use a different ground image (finished file, base.png, image.png), so every mode switch decodes a different full-res PNG in the WebView.
scenario: Switching modes on large screenshots causes repeated full-resolution decodes and delays.
fix: No specific fix given.

votes.evidence: ShotViewer.tsx:439-448: `const ground = mode === "crop" ? { src: edit?.originalPath ?? clip.path, ...full } : mode === "draw" ? { src: edit?.basePath ?? clip.path, ... } : { src: clip.path, ... }`, fed to one (840-841). commands.rs:466-476: `base_path: if base.is_file() { Some(base) } else if original.is_file() { Some(original) } else { None }`, `original_path: original.is_file().then(..)`; comment 'Untouched so far: the clip's own file is both grounds at once.' ShotViewer.tsx:366-367 documents the three grounds as intentional.
votes.corrected_claim: Only edited screenshots get different grounds. An untouched shot has basePath and originalPath set to null, so view, draw and crop all load the same clip.path URL and nothing extra is decoded. A shot with marks only has basePath equal to image.png, so draw and crop share one file (two distinct images in total). Three distinct full-resolution files (the finished file, base.png and image.png) appear only after a crop. Each is needed by design: the finished file, the cropped picture without marks, and the whole original. Whether a return to a recently shown file decodes again depends on Chromium's image memory cache.
votes.reachable_by: A user switching between view, draw and crop on a screenshot that has already been edited (cropped, or for two files marked).
votes.fix_assessment: No fix was proposed, and the cost is inherent: each mode has to show a different picture. At most the images could be preloaded or kept decoded (for example hidden elements or createImageBitmap) to hide the latency.

title: OpenClipboard called with a NULL owner window (unsupported for SetClipboardData)
claim: The clipboard is opened with `OpenClipboard(HWND::default())`. MSDN says that with a NULL owner, `EmptyClipboard` sets the owner to NULL and `SetClipboardData` "fails". It works in practice, but it's unsupported.
scenario: On some Windows configurations SetClipboardData could fail after EmptyClipboard with a NULL owner, breaking Copy picture/text.
fix: Pass the main window's HWND to OpenClipboard.

votes.evidence: src-tauri/src/clipboard.rs:43 `if unsafe { OpenClipboard(HWND::default()) }.is_ok()`, followed by `EmptyClipboard()` and `SetClipboardData(format, ...)` in copy_files/copy_image/copy_text (121-123, 132-134, 144-146; put() at 76). Callers: commands.rs:667, 799, 888, 907 and links.rs:332, 398. The code does open the clipboard with a NULL owner and then empties it. The MSDN remark the finding cites (with a NULL owner, EmptyClipboard makes the owner NULL and SetClipboardData fails) is documentation that cannot be checked from this sandbox (the windows crate is not in ~/.cargo/registry). In practice SetClipboardData with immediate (non-delayed) data succeeds with a NULL owner on current Windows, and widely used clipboard crates do the same.
votes.corrected_claim: The code fact is correct: a NULL owner HWND is passed. The failure scenario is speculative. Nothing in the repo shows a failure, and the finding itself says it works in practice. Whether some Windows configuration rejects SetClipboardData here depends on Win32 behaviour that cannot be checked from source.
votes.reachable_by: Copy picture, copy file, copy text and copy link actions. A failure would only show up if Windows actually enforced the documented restriction.
votes.fix_assessment: Passing the main window's HWND is harmless and follows the documentation. Note that the window then receives WM_DESTROYCLIPBOARD, and the HWND must still be valid when the call is made (e.g. not while the window is being torn down).

title: External edits to the screenshot are silently overwritten on the next ClippiBoy save
claim: `edit_screenshot` rebuilds from the stored original (`image.png`) every time (commands.rs:539) without checking whether the main file was changed externally; the DB dimensions also go stale.
scenario: After the first ClippiBoy edit, the user edits the PNG in Paint or Photos. The next ClippiBoy save rebuilds from the stale image.png and drops those external changes.
fix: Record size and mtime (or a hash) of the last written file in shot.json; on mismatch warn, or adopt the external file as the new original.

title: Blocking sync commands marked #[tauri::command(async)] run on tokio workers
claim: `write_screenshot`, `copy_clip_image` and `take_screenshot` are sync fns with `#[tauri::command(async)]`, which (likely, per Tauri 2.11 macro behaviour) runs them on async runtime workers. They do blocking work there: PNG decode/encode, blur loops, `replace_file`'s sleep-retry (up to about 2.75 s), the blocking ffmpeg wait, and `Clipboard::open`'s sleeps.
scenario: A slow save or clipboard retry stalls other async tasks sharing the runtime (share, links, updater).
fix: Make them `async fn` and wrap the body in `tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking`.

title: Sidecars committed before the main PNG; several screenshot writes are not atomic
claim: In edit_screenshot the write order is `shot.write_png(&base_path)` (`File::create` truncates base.png in place), then `write_edit(...)` (shot.json), then `write_picture` (temp + `replace_file`, retried 10x then fails with "Is it open somewhere right now?"). The comment at commands.rs:555 ("Everything that can fail happens before the first byte is written") is not true for these three writes. `keep_original` copies to `image.png` with a plain `std::fs::copy`, and `write_under` writes `under.png`/`under.json` non-atomically as well.
scenario: (a) The screenshot is open in an external viewer that locks it, or AV holds it: `replace_file` fails, but base.png and shot.json already describe the new crop and marks while the PNG is the old one; the UI catches the error and keeps its old `edit`, so the next open shows a state the file doesn't have. (b) Disk full while writing base.png leaves a truncated base.png, so draw mode shows "File not found". (c) A crash or disk-full during `keep_original`'s `std::fs::copy` leaves a partial image.png; `has_original` is then true forever and every later edit, including Reset, fails in `read_png(original)`.
fix: Write all three to temp names first (`base.png.part`, `shot.json.part`, `<name>.<uuid>.new.png`). Then `replace_file` the main PNG (most likely to fail); only on success rename the sidecar parts (or remove base.png); on failure delete the parts. `keep_original`: copy to `image.png.part` and rename. `write_under`: same for under.png and under.json.

title: Save racing a file move or delete orphans the edited PNG and leaves the DB pointing at the unedited file
claim: `edit_screenshot` reads `clip.path` once at the start (commands.rs:518) and writes to it about 0.5-2 s later; nothing locks the clip. Closing the viewer runs `for (const id of seen) if (left.has(id)) void fileClip(id);` (Clips.tsx), and `file_clip` moves the file (favorites or game folder) and updates the DB path. The viewer's close button, Escape after Discard, and the footer Delete button all stay enabled while `busy`.
scenario: The user changes the game or hits the heart in the viewer, clicks Save marks, and closes right away. `filing::place` renames P1 to P2 (and may prune P1's folder); `write_picture` then creates a new file at P1 (rename onto a missing target succeeds) and runs `set_picture` with the edited dimensions. Result: the DB points at the unedited P2 with wrong dimensions, the thumbnail comes from the orphan at P1, and P1 stays in the user's folder forever. Delete during a save similarly recreates `originals/<id>/…` and the PNG as orphans.
fix: Add a per-clip busy set in `AppState`: `write_screenshot` holds it; `file_clip` and `delete_clip` wait for it or skip. Re-read `lib.get(id).path` immediately before `replace_file`, inside the library lock. Disable Close and Delete while `busy`, or defer `fileClip` until the save resolves.

also.title: edit_screenshot has no save lock
also.claim: The clip editor serialises its saves with `WORKING` (edit.rs:48-53), but `edit_screenshot` (commands.rs:511-599) has no lock. The UI's `busy` flag is the only guard against concurrent saves of the same screenshot.
also.fix: Add a save lock for `edit_screenshot` like the clip editor's `WORKING`.

title: Editor usable before its edit store loads; failed load swallowed; save then drops crop/marks and misplaces blurs
claim: The load is `api.screenshotEdit(id).then(...).catch(() => {})` and tools are enabled with `disabled={!inTauri || broken}` with no check of `edit`. While `edit` is null: `full = clip.width` (the cropped size), `origin = {0,0}`, draw mode draws on `clip.path` (marks already baked in), and Save sends `write(edit?.crop ?? null, shapes)`, i.e. crop = null. If the load resolves late, `resetShapes(readMarks(loaded))` silently wipes whatever was drawn in the meantime.
scenario: `screenshot_edit` errors (e.g. "clip database is not available") or resolves late because the main thread is busy. On a cropped shot with only blur marks, saving silently removes the crop, drops previously saved marks from shot.json, and applies the crop-relative blur rectangles to the uncropped original at the wrong spot, so the redaction misses its target. With non-blur marks Rust fails with "The layer does not fit the picture."
fix: Disable tools and Save until `edit !== null`; show the load error instead of swallowing it; have `write` refuse to run while `edit` is null.

also.title: Swallowed screenshotEdit failure makes the next save drop the crop and misplace marks
also.claim: If loading the existing edit via `screenshotEdit` fails, the error is swallowed (ShotViewer.tsx:341-356). A later save (1066) then sends `crop: null` with marks positioned on the cropped picture, which drops the crop and puts the marks in the wrong place.
also.fix: No explicit fix proposed in the report.

title: Save's async continuation is not tied to the clip it started for; old edit lands on the next picture
claim: After `await writeScreenshot(...)` the code runs `const loaded = await api.screenshotEdit(clip.id); setEdit(loaded); resetShapes(readMarks(loaded));` using the closure's (old) `clip`, with no check that the viewer still shows it. Discard is always enabled (1089) and the step/navigation buttons are enabled once `mode === "view"` (1249, 1259).
scenario: Save, then Discard (mode -> view), then navigate to the next shot. The new shot's load resolves fast; the old continuation resolves later and wins, so the viewer holds the previous screenshot's `edit` (its `basePath`, crop and marks) for the new picture. Entering draw mode shows the wrong base; saving writes the foreign crop and marks into the new screenshot.
fix: Keep `const shownId = useRef(id)` and bail out after each await when `shownId.current !== clip.id`. Better: have `write_screenshot` return the new `ShotEdit` directly.

title: Marks drawn while a save is running are silently discarded
claim: AnnotateLayer stays interactive while `busy` (ShotViewer.tsx:880-892). When the save finishes, `resetShapes(readMarks(loaded)); … setMode("view")` (632-638) replaces everything drawn since Save was clicked.
scenario: On a 4K picture (about a 1 s save) the user adds one more arrow right after clicking Save; the arrow vanishes without a prompt and there is no undo.
fix: Block input while `busy` (`pointer-events: none` overlay or BusyVeil), or snapshot `current.current` at save time and re-apply any newer shapes as unsaved.

also.title: Marks drawn during a running save are overwritten
also.claim: While a screenshot save runs (0.5-2 s for a 4K picture), the annotate and crop layers stay interactive: no busy flag is passed to `AnnotateLayer`/`CropLayer` (ShotViewer.tsx:880-892), and keys are not ignored. When the save finishes, `resetShapes(readMarks(loaded))` (ShotViewer.tsx:634) replaces the shapes with the saved state, so marks and undo actions made during the save are silently overwritten.
also.fix: Pass `busy` to `AnnotateLayer` and `CropLayer` (`pointer-events-none`, plus a `BusyRing` overlay) and ignore keys while busy. Or compare `current.current` with the shapes that were sent and keep anything newer.

title: PNG decompression bomb in read_png/read_rgba (allocation before any size check), reachable via friend-shared screenshots
claim: `read_png` allocates the frame buffer from IHDR alone: `let mut buffer = vec![0u8; reader.output_buffer_size()];` (shot.rs:455-472); png 0.17's `Limits` only cap row and chunk buffers, not this caller-allocated buffer. `read_rgba` (shot.rs:676-689) checks the layer's dimensions against the picture only after the full allocation and decode (`blend`, shot.rs:105-108). Received shared files go straight into the library (share.rs:633-692).
scenario: A malicious or compromised friend sends a ~100-byte "screenshot" whose IHDR claims 60000x60000 (about 14 GB RGBA). The user right-clicks it and chooses Copy picture (`copy_clip_image`) or edits it; `vec!` fails and `handle_alloc_error` aborts the whole app, replay buffer included. If the allocation succeeds instead, the RGB conversion and `dib()` allocate another 2-3x.
fix: After `read_info`, reject anything with `w as u64 * h as u64 > 1<<28` (and dimensions > 16384), then allocate with `try_reserve_exact`. Give `read_rgba` the expected `(w, h)` and reject on mismatch before allocating. At receive time read the header and store the real dimensions.

title: Layer PNGs travel over IPC as JSON number arrays and are buffered by serde as Content
claim: `layerBytes` returns `Array.from(new Uint8Array(await blob.arrayBuffer()))`, so each byte becomes about 3.6 JSON characters plus a JS Number, stringified on the UI thread. On the Rust side `Step` is internally tagged (`#[serde(tag = "kind")] … Layer { png: Vec<u8> }`), so serde first buffers the whole object into `Content` (one ~32-byte `Content::U64` per PNG byte) and then copies into `Vec<u8>`.
scenario: A 2 MB layer (text-heavy, large fills, 8K) costs roughly 7 MB of JSON plus 64 MB of transient Rust memory per save.
fix: Send layers as raw IPC bodies (`invoke("write_shot_layer", bytes, { headers: { id, index } })`, Rust reads `tauri::ipc::Request` -> `InvokeBody::Raw`), or at minimum base64 strings with `#[serde(with = "...")]` and an adjacently/externally tagged enum. Encode in a worker with `OffscreenCanvas.convertToBlob`.

also.title: Layer PNGs travel over IPC as JSON number arrays
also.claim: Each layer's PNG bytes are sent as a JSON `number[]` via `Array.from(Uint8Array)` (ShotViewer.tsx:1623; types.ts:525-527; commands.rs:400-419), roughly 3-4x the bytes plus parse time. Tauri 2 accepts raw bodies (`tauri::ipc::Request` / `InvokeBody::Raw`) and can return raw bytes (`tauri::ipc::Response`).
also.fix: Send `Uint8Array` as a raw invoke body and read it in Rust through `tauri::ipc::Request`; change the `ShotStep.layer.png` type.

title: Preview and save use full-resolution canvases per blur-separated run
claim: Preview canvases are `<canvas width={width} height={height}>` at full picture pixels (ShotAnnotate.tsx:566-586). Every blur splits the layer runs, so N blurs mean N+1 canvases of 3840x2160 (33 MB each; 132 MB each at 8K) plus the draft canvas. Save allocates another N full-size canvases at once (`Promise.all(... layerBytes ...)`, ShotViewer.tsx:609-618); at 8K this can fail, and `getContext`/`toBlob` returning null throws and is swallowed (see the swallowed-failures finding).
scenario: On 4K/8K screenshots with several blurs, the WebView holds hundreds of MB of canvas memory; saving at 8K can fail silently.
fix: Size preview canvases to `round(box.width*devicePixelRatio)` with `ctx.setTransform(scale…)`, repainting on zoom. Serialise `layerBytes` (or use OffscreenCanvas in a worker).

also.title: Preview memory grows with blur count (one full-res canvas per layer)
also.claim: Each run of marks is its own full-resolution preview canvas (ShotAnnotate.tsx:566-586), and each blur splits the run. A 4K canvas is about 33 MB, so 10 blurs interleaved with marks is about 11 canvases, roughly 360 MB. The export path (`layerBytes`, ShotViewer.tsx:1607-1624) then encodes one full-size PNG per layer.
also.fix: Single WebView renderer (option A) with cached bitmaps below/above the active mark and display-resolution preview.
